question: How does S.C. Code Section 50-21-10 define a "vessel" for purposes of South Carolina's boating chapter?
choice_a: Every description of watercraft, other than a seaplane regulated by the federal government, used or capable of being used as a means of transportation on water
choice_b: Only craft that are federally documented
choice_d: Any structure permanently fixed to the shoreline
explanation: Section 50-21-10 defines "vessel" broadly as every description of watercraft, other than a federally regulated seaplane, used or capable of being used as a means of transportation on water, a definition wide enough to cover everything from a canoe to a large cabin cruiser.

question: Under Section 50-21-10, which items are specifically excluded from the statutory definition of "watercraft"?
choice_a: Nothing is ever excluded from the definition of watercraft
choice_b: Only vessels over 65 feet are excluded
choice_c: Water skis, aquaplanes, surfboards, windsurfers, tubes, rafts, and similar devices, along with seaplanes, are excluded from the "watercraft" definition even though some of them are separately regulated elsewhere in the chapter
explanation: Section 50-21-10 defines "watercraft" as anything used or capable of being used as a means of transportation on water, but specifically carves out seaplanes and towed/human-powered recreational items such as water skis, aquaplanes, surfboards, windsurfers, tubes, and rafts, which are instead addressed by the chapter's separate water-skiing provisions.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. Section 50-21-10 (definition of "watercraft" and its exclusions)

question: Under Section 50-21-10, how broadly does South Carolina law define the term "operate" as applied to a vessel or watercraft?
choice_a: It applies only to a person physically holding a steering wheel
choice_b: It has no defined meaning in the statute
choice_c: To navigate, steer, drive, or be in control, a definition that also extends to manipulating moving water skis, a moving aquaplane, a moving surfboard, or a similar moving device
choice_d: It applies only to commercial vessel captains
explanation: Section 50-21-10 defines "operate" broadly to mean navigating, steering, driving, or otherwise being in control of a vessel, and it explicitly extends this control concept to a person manipulating a moving water ski, aquaplane, surfboard, or similar device, tying that towed activity back into the chapter's operator-focused rules.

question: How does Section 50-21-10 define an "owner" of a vessel or outboard motor?
choice_a: Only a bank or lienholder financing the purchase
choice_b: A person, other than a lienholder, who claims lawful possession of a vessel or outboard motor by virtue of legal title or equitable interest
choice_c: Only the person who most recently operated the vessel
choice_d: Whoever is physically aboard the vessel at a given moment
explanation: Section 50-21-10 defines "owner" as a person, other than a lienholder, who claims lawful possession of a vessel or outboard motor through legal title or an equitable interest, distinguishing true ownership from a lender's security interest or a temporary operator's control.

question: According to Section 50-21-10, what is a "marina" under South Carolina's boating chapter?
choice_a: Any body of water regardless of facilities
choice_b: A facility that provides mooring or dry storage for watercraft
choice_c: A term reserved exclusively for U.S. Coast Guard installations
choice_d: Only a facility that sells fuel
explanation: Section 50-21-10 defines a "marina" as a facility that provides mooring or dry storage for watercraft, a definition broad enough to cover everything from a full-service marina with fuel and repair services to a simple dry-stack storage yard.

question: How does Section 50-21-10 define a "marine dealer" in South Carolina?
choice_a: Only a manufacturer that builds vessels overseas
choice_b: A business that engages in buying or selling, exchanging, brokering, manufacturing, or servicing watercraft or outboard motors
choice_c: Any individual boat owner who sells a personal vessel once
explanation: Section 50-21-10 defines a "marine dealer" as a business engaged in buying, selling, exchanging, brokering, manufacturing, or servicing watercraft or outboard motors, a commercial-activity definition distinct from a private individual selling their own boat.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. Section 50-21-10 (definition of "marine dealer")

question: Under Section 50-21-10, what makes a propulsion unit an "outboard motor" rather than an inboard engine?
choice_a: Whether the motor is gasoline- or diesel-powered
choice_b: Whether the motor was manufactured in the United States
choice_c: Whether it is a combustion engine or electric propulsion system used to propel a watercraft that is detachable from the watercraft as a unit
choice_d: Whether the motor is painted black
explanation: Section 50-21-10 defines an "outboard motor" as a combustion engine or electric propulsion system used to propel a watercraft that is detachable from the watercraft as a complete unit, capturing the key structural distinction from a fixed inboard engine mounted inside the hull.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. Section 50-21-10 (definition of "outboard motor")
